text:
Maya: Heads-up — customer reported ~2x token billing for a single user action when a streaming websocket reconnects during an external action (tool invocation). Looks like truncation + fallback routing together are causing provisional and final token counts to both be booked.

Jon: Ugh. Do we have logs or a repro trace?

Maya: Pasting sanitized snippet below. Happened on prod route us-west-2, model pinned to gpt-open-3.

```
[INFO] 2026-03-19T15:02:11Z stream_id=st_9 session_id=sess_42 user_id=acct_77 model=gpt-open-3 route=us-west-2 fallback=true resume=ws-reconnect resume_offset=128 truncation=tool-timeout external_call_id=tool_19 tokens_charged=420 provisional_tokens=720
[DEBUG] 2026-03-19T15:02:11Z ledger_entry provisional=true session_seq=3 idempotency_key=session:sess_42:seq:3
[INFO] 2026-03-19T15:02:12Z final_ack received final_tokens=418 shrink_adjust=false
```

Maya: The ledger shows provisional_tokens=720 then a final_ack with final_tokens=418 but we didn't retract the provisional charge; customer sees net +302 tokens.

Prashant: @Maya thanks — is the provisional record missing a link to the final record? Looks like our provisional write happens at stream resume (to avoid undercharging) but we never compact/reconcile when the final ACK comes in if the session_seq has been re-routed. Could be a session_seq mismatch after fallback routing.

Olga: Quick q — are these tool-invocations using our current external-invocation TTL? We recently shortened TTLs on the cheaper routing to force truncation faster. That could cause more resumptions and provisional bookings.

Maya: Yes TTL was 7s on fallback path, primary path 30s. Customer triggered a heavy external call, fallback happened, WS reconnected, runtime re-routed to cheaper pool which truncates the stream and we emit provisional ledger entries during reconnect handoff.

Jon: Two things we need to decide: (1) short-term mitigation to prevent customers from seeing doubled charges, (2) longer-term invariants so ledger is idempotent across reconnects/fallbacks.

Prashant: Proposals: 
- A: Mark provisional ledger entries with "provisional_session_id" and tie them to final session_seq; run an async reconciler that emits a negative adjustment if final < provisional.
- B: Make provisional entries non-billing (show in Console as "provisional tokens") and only bill on final ACK. UX: Console shows provisional estimate in gray and final in bold.
- C: Add resume_seq sequence numbers to telemetry and require idempotent consume by ledger service; if mismatch, hold provisional for X minutes instead of immediately booking.

Olga: I like B for user-facing safety. We can show provisional in Console and API telemetry so support can explain. But operationally we need a provisioning window to avoid customers getting undercharged while final ACK never comes. Maybe provisional should convert to bill after 10 minutes if no final ACK, with alerts to SRE.

Jon: Implementation effort: 
- Billing-service: accept "provisional=true/false" flag, store provisional records separately and support negative adjustments. (~3d). Owner: @Prashant
- Console: display provisional vs final tokens on per-request trace and per-customer analytics. Need UX + backend change. (~2w). Owner: @Olga
- Runtime: emit session_seq + resume_reason on all resume events and include idempotency_key in ledger writes. (~5d). Owner: @Maya

billing-bot: Creating ticket BW-5123 for provisional-ledger work (priority P0).

deploy-bot: Ran canary for provisional-ledger flag on staging. All checks passed.

Prashant: Short-term quickfix: credit back customers matched by session_id if we detect duplicate booking within 1h. I can prototype a reconciler that scans provisional vs final and emits credits. That avoids a Console change immediately.

Jon: OK short-term plan: implement reconciler + auto-credit within 1h window, coupled with a support dashboard query to find affected accounts. Long-term: B + C (provisional UX + telemetry + idempotent ledger).

Maya: I'll open a follow-up PR to runtime to include resume_seq and explicit resume_reason tags. Also logging change to include "provisional_id" written by ledger so we can trace easier.

Olga: I'll scope the Console changes and mock a UI showing "Provisional estimate" next to token count. Also will add a tooltip explaining fallback/truncation.

Prashant: I'll own the billing-service PR and the reconciler job. Will post a design doc by EOD.

Jon: Thanks folks. @billing-bot can you post a weekly report for BW-5123 until resolved and route to CS for any impacted customers? :thumbsup:

billing-bot: Will do — adding BW-5123 to weekly billing report and pinging #customer-success if credits posted.

Maya: Quick note — we should also add a telemetry counter for "resume->final_mismatch" so we can create an alert if this pattern spikes.

Prashant: Added to TODOs.

Jon: Awesome. We'll reconvene after the reconciler prototype.
